summary: A clinician (often a GI-trained physician, dietitian, nurse or pharmacist) who interprets gut microbiome data and delivers or coordinates microbiome-targeted care: diet plans, probiotics, and regulated live biotherapeutics such as FDA-approved Rebyota and Vowst or FMT for recurrent C. difficile. AI helps most in turning noisy sequencing reports into cautious plain-language summaries, tracking an evidence base that changes quickly, keeping documentation and consent compliant, and separating proven indications from marketing claims.

prompts.title: Translate a microbiome test report
prompts.task: Turn a lab or direct-to-consumer stool sequencing report into a careful clinical summary and patient explanation
prompts.prompt: You are assisting a microbiome therapist. Below is a de-identified stool microbiome report from [LAB/TEST NAME] using [16S rRNA / SHOTGUN METAGENOMICS], for a patient with [PRESENTING CONDITION]. [PASTE REPORT]. Produce: (1) a clinician summary table listing each finding, what the method can and cannot resolve (taxonomic level, relative vs absolute abundance), and the strength of evidence linking it to the condition (strong / emerging / speculative); (2) a 150-word plain-language explanation for the patient that avoids implying diagnosis; (3) findings that warrant standard work-up instead (e.g. calprotectin, C. diff testing, colonoscopy referral). Flag any reference ranges whose provenance is unclear.
prompts.caution: Most consumer microbiome tests are not validated diagnostics; do not change medication or diagnose based on them alone.

prompts.title: Recurrent C. diff therapy options brief
prompts.task: Compare guideline-supported options for a patient with recurrent C. difficile infection
prompts.prompt: Act as a clinical evidence assistant. My patient has had [NUMBER] C. difficile episodes; prior treatments: [LIST]; comorbidities: [LIST, e.g. immunosuppression, IBD]; setting: [COUNTRY/HEALTH SYSTEM]. Using the IDSA/SHEA 2021 focused update, ACG 2021 guidance and the FDA labels for fecal microbiota live-jslm (Rebyota) and fecal microbiota spores live-brpk (Vowst), compare options (fidaxomicin, vancomycin taper, bezlotoxumab status, approved microbiome products, conventional FMT under FDA enforcement discretion or local rules). Output a table: option, eligibility, key evidence, safety concerns, logistics/cost. Note where your knowledge may be outdated and what I should verify against current labels.
prompts.caution: Check current labels and guidance; bezlotoxumab was discontinued in the US in 2025 and product availability varies by country.

prompts.title: Donor screening protocol gap check
prompts.task: Audit a stool donor screening SOP against published consensus
prompts.prompt: You are a quality reviewer for a stool donor program at [INSTITUTION]. Here is our donor screening and testing SOP: [PASTE SOP]. Compare it against the FDA safety communications on FMT (including MDRO and SARS-CoV-2/mpox screening alerts), the 2019 international consensus on stool banking (Gut), and, if we operate in the EU, the SoHO Regulation (EU) 2024/1938. Produce a gap table: requirement, source, our current practice, gap severity (critical/major/minor), suggested fix. List requirements you are unsure of separately, and do not invent clauses or citation numbers.
prompts.caution: Final protocol decisions belong to the program's medical director and regulatory/IRB oversight.

prompts.title: Personalized diet-microbiome plan
prompts.task: Draft a 6-week dietary intervention plan with monitoring checkpoints
prompts.prompt: You are helping a microbiome therapist working with a registered dietitian. Patient: [AGE, SEX], diagnosis [e.g. IBS-D, post-antibiotic dysbiosis], current diet [SUMMARY], restrictions [ALLERGIES, CULTURAL/RELIGIOUS], medications [LIST]. Draft a 6-week plan (e.g. fiber diversification, low-FODMAP with structured reintroduction, fermented foods) as a weekly table: goals, specific foods/servings, symptom metrics to log, and red-flag symptoms needing medical review. Cite the trial or guideline behind each element and grade its evidence. Flag interactions or contraindications (e.g. fiber with strictures, fermented foods when immunocompromised).
prompts.caution: Low-FODMAP and restrictive diets carry malnutrition and disordered-eating risk; coordinate with a dietitian.

prompts.title: Probiotic claim fact-check
prompts.task: Evaluate a supplement or company's microbiome claims for a patient or clinic newsletter
prompts.prompt: A patient asked about [PRODUCT NAME], which claims: [PASTE CLAIMS]. Act as a skeptical evidence reviewer. For each claim: identify the strain(s) at strain level, whether strain-specific RCTs exist, population and outcome studied, and whether the claim matches the evidence (supported / partially / unsupported). Note its regulatory status (US dietary supplement under DSHEA with structure/function claims vs approved drug) and any relevant AGA 2020 or World Gastroenterology Organisation probiotic guidance. Finish with a 100-word neutral answer I can give the patient. Say clearly when you cannot verify a study exists.
prompts.caution: Do not cite studies you cannot verify; check references in PubMed before sharing.

prompts.title: Informed consent and patient handout
prompts.task: Draft consent and aftercare material for a microbiome procedure
prompts.prompt: Draft an informed consent document and a one-page aftercare handout for [PROCEDURE, e.g. FMT via colonoscopy / oral capsule live biotherapeutic] at [CLINIC TYPE, COUNTRY]. Reading level: grade 6-8. Include: purpose, regulatory status (approved product vs investigational/enforcement discretion), known risks including infection transmission and unknown long-term effects, alternatives, what donor screening covers and cannot rule out, data/sample retention, and when to call or seek emergency care. Output in plain headings with [CLINIC CONTACT] placeholders. Mark sections our legal or IRB team must review.
prompts.caution: Consent forms need institutional legal/IRB review; investigational use may require an IND.

prompts.title: Adverse event and outcomes log review
prompts.task: Analyze a clinic's treatment outcomes and adverse events for trends and reporting duties
prompts.prompt: You are a clinical quality analyst. Here is our de-identified outcomes log for [TREATMENT] over [DATE RANGE] with columns [LIST COLUMNS]: [PASTE DATA]. Calculate cure/recurrence rates at 8 weeks, adverse event frequency by type and severity, and any donor- or batch-linked clusters. Identify events that may require reporting (FDA MedWatch, IND safety reports, or [LOCAL AUTHORITY]) and flag them for my review. Present a summary table, a short trend narrative, and limitations (sample size, missing follow-up, confounders). Do not infer causation without stating uncertainty.
prompts.caution: Remove identifiers before pasting; reporting decisions rest with the responsible clinician.

prompts.title: Field upskilling plan
prompts.task: Build a learning plan to keep up with a fast-moving microbiome evidence base
prompts.prompt: I am a [BACKGROUND, e.g. gastroenterology nurse practitioner / dietitian] moving into microbiome-based care, with [HOURS] hours per week for [MONTHS] months. Build a learning plan covering: sequencing methods and their limits (16S vs shotgun, compositional data analysis), host-microbe mechanisms, live biotherapeutic regulation (FDA CBER, EMA, EU SoHO), C. diff and IBD/IBS trial evidence, and critical appraisal of microbiome studies. Format as a month-by-month table with resources (textbooks, society courses such as AGA/ISAPP, review papers by topic rather than invented titles), a hands-on exercise, and a self-test question each month. List open scientific questions I should track.
